### 1) What is on the screen
The frame shows a night ship-deck test background at 256x240: dark blue star sky in [0,0,256,34], bright blue sea band in [0,34,220,26], white rail fence in [0,70,256,14], grey plank deck in [0,84,220,38], a solid black vertical mast/piling in [220,32,26,90], two small black deck-houses in [18,16,16,14] and [86,16,16,14], and a tiny white moon in [202,2,9,9]. The eye goes first to the white railing band in [0,70,256,14] because it is the only high-contrast horizontal. What the player is being asked to do I cannot see - no player sprite, enemy, HUD, objective marker, or text prompt is visible.

### 2) Does it look like a real NES game
(a) palette count reads as NES - PASS: 7 distinct colours, measured all in the 64-entry NES palette and inside the 25 colours on screen ceiling (12 BG + 12 sprite + 1 backdrop), reads as 2 BG palettes + backdrop.
(b) shading is flat, one colour per shape - PASS: sky, sea, rail, planks are flat fills, no gradient banding I can see.
(c) sprites read at a glance against background - FAIL: I cannot see any sprites; there is no player/enemy silhouette to read, frame is background-only.
(d) no anti-aliasing and no soft edges - PASS: all edges, stars in [0,0,256,34] and rail posts are hard 1px, no soft text/window borders I can see.
(e) colour changes land on 16x16 grid - FAIL: horizontal bands are full-width and OK, but the black mast edge at x~220 in [220,32,26,90] is not on a 16-pixel boundary and its 26px width is not a whole number of 8px tiles, so it would force attribute bleed if BG. Measured numbers do not contradict this - 7 colours and 57.8% single-colour coverage match an unfinished but technically legal file.

### 3) Composition and text
Crowded in the top strip [0,0,256,122] where sky/sea/rail/deck are all squeezed; empty in the bottom [0,122,256,118] which is solid black and accounts for the measured 57.8% dominant colour. The focal point (white rail) is not where the player needs it - the lower half where action would be is void. Text legibility: I cannot see any text regions at 256x240. Worst text region: none present, which is itself the failure - no HUD, score, or prompt to read without guessing.

### 4) What looks AI generated or off
This does not read as typical AI mush - no pillow shading, no morphing detail, no gibberish glyphs, edges are hard and palette is honestly limited to 7 NES entries. It reads as a handmade programmer tile-test, but unfinished and off: 1) massive unfinished black void in [0,122,256,118]; 2) star field in [0,0,256,34] looks randomly scattered single pixels, not built from repeating 8x8 tiles; 3) right mast in [220,32,26,90] not tile-multiple and just stops mid-air with no base/cap structure; 4) moon in [202,2,9,9] isolated with no tile structure; 5) composition reads as stacked bands, not a designed playfield - no ground line for the player to stand on.

### 5) Five concrete fixes
1. Region [0,122,256,118]: fill the black void - replace NES $0F black fill with continuing deck tiles using one BG palette: backdrop $0F black, $00 dark grey for planks, $10 light grey for plank highlights, $12 dark blue for seams. No large flat black remains.
2. Region [220,32,26,90]: snap mast to tile grid - move 4px right to [224,32,16,88], shrink width from 26 to 16 (2x whole 8px tiles), redraw as 16x88 BG column using $0F black + $00 grey edge highlight, 16-pixel aligned in x.
3. Region [8,8,120,8]: add HUD text row - redraw from blank to 8x8 white NES $30 font on $12 dark-blue strip: "HP SCORE TIME", 15 glyphs, all glyphs on 8px cell boundaries.
4. Region [0,0,256,32]: rebuild stars as tiles - keep only 8 star positions on 8x8 grid, erase other single-pixel stars, use NES $30 white 1px on $02 very dark blue, repeat same two 8x8 star tiles across row.
5. Region [112,86,16,32]: add player anchor sprite - place one 8x16 sprite (2 tiles) standing on deck line, sprite palette: transparent + NES $30 white + $16 red + $0F black outline, to give the rail/deck a focal point to read against BG.

### 6) Scores and machine readable block
NES Authenticity: 6/10
Readability: 3/10
Charm: 3/10
